text: Here is a three-part hypothesis on long-term codebase degradation. Second, if AI readily invents ad-hoc wrapper functions to solve immediate local friction, then the effective API surface area will expand exponentially, inflating maintenance overhead without adding functional value. Third, if code and documentation are updated independently per prompt without a persistent global model, then doc-code divergence will accelerate, causing automated systems to misinterpret historical invariants over multi-year lifecycles.
coreIdea: Semantic entropy and ephemeral abstraction accumulation
observableConsequence: An exponential increase in unhandled edge-case exceptions and a measurable rise in dead wrapper utilities detected via static analysis tools within eighteen months of heavy AI integration across enterprise repositories.
counterevidence: Codebases utilizing heavy AI-assisted generation exhibit lower rates of undocumented wrapper accumulation and maintain stable exception-handling variance over a three-year observation period compared to unassisted legacy codebases.
